English: Taki the Beer-maker was still sleeping, even though the sun’s rays had long since pierced the clouded, grimy windows of his stuffy room; the rays gradually illuminated his legs, then crept up toward his potbelly, shone on his lower lip, which was dried and cracked from an internal fire; then they moved toward his open mouth and penetrated down his throat, from which emanated waves of snoring, deafening to the ear. Just then, the postman knocked three times at the door; but don’t imagine that Taki’s ear comprehends such gentle signals. Had it been a workday, well, then, maybe, but this was a holiday; and on the eve of a holiday, you know, a person lets himself go a bit more. You clink glasses with this guy, you clink glasses with that guy, and eventually you get completely clinked out! That’s just what had happened to Bai Taki. In his desire to promote his beer, he got himself pickled. My point is that you won’t be surprised that the postman repeated his knocking on the door. But when no one appeared, he delivered to that totally innocent door such a hard, merciless pounding that even if Bai Taki’s stomach had met up with an entire vat of beer, he would’ve woken up; and wake up he did. He opened his eyes, blinked in the sunlight, and, in a voice worthy of the throat whence it emanated, asked, “Who’s there?” “The mail,” answered the postman. He entered the room, crossed over to the bed, handed over a letter, and hastened to escape the stifling atmosphere of the unventilated bedroom. Bai Taki coughed for a little while, as was his habit, rubbed his eyes, and opened the letter. An invitation!
